title: My first ever game jam with Claude Code
author: SvitsGames
selftext:
![video](g6cgkj03gy3i1 "Cave II, cleared on the 6th try. Every lantern you see is a spot where I failed")

So I did my first game jam ever last weekend ([Foundplay Jam #1](https://foundplay.io/jams/foundplay-jam-1), the theme was "One more try"), and since I made the whole thing with Claude Code I thought I'd share how that went.

The game is called Trylight. It's a one-button runner in dark caves. You can barely see what's coming, but every time you fail, a lantern stays lit where it happened, so the more you fail, the more of the cave you can see.

Claude Code wrote the code, the levels and the in-game text. I made the design decisions and played every build (a lot). The visuals are just silhouettes and glow drawn in code, and the music and sounds are synthesised in code too. The whole game is a 432 KB zip.

# What (kinda) worked:

1. **Let the AI play the game itself**. The game rules (jumping, hitting things) are kept separate from the graphics, so Claude can run the game without drawing anything. At first it only used that to check each cave could be beaten, and **it completely missed a jump in cave III that killed me every single time**. Beatable isn't the same as fair. Once I told it, it added a second check for jumps that are too hard to time, and that one found three more in caves I hadn't even gotten to yet.

2. **Make the endless mode out of safe pieces**. After the eight caves there's an endless cave, a new one every day. It isn't random terrain. It glues together short bits of the normal caves, and each bit is checked to be beatable. So it's different every day, but you never get a part that can't be done (hopefully).

3. **Just say what's wrong in normal words.** My notes were things like "a new player dies in 5 seconds" or "the sound crackles on my phone". For the first one, the runner now stops right before the first spike if you don't press anything, and waits for you to jump. For the crackle, it figured out my phone couldn't keep up with the echo effect and set up the sound differently on phones. Crackle gone.

4. **Keep a notes file**. One file lists everything I've decided and why, another says what's done and what's next. Every new chat starts by reading them, so it doesn't forget things I'd already decided, like no yellow anywhere or no double jump (tried it, it did not really land).

**And it was a lot of back and forth.** I played every build and kept asking for changes: the endless mode, the countdown before every run, the game filling the whole screen and turning sideways on phones, a menu with stats for every cave. It tested a lot in a headless browser, but it couldn't hear the crackle, or tell that half a second per number in the countdown was too fast.

**If you want to try it, it runs in the browser, no sign-in:** [**foundplay link**](https://foundplay.io/games/trylight?utm_source=creator)

I'm not done with it yet. I really like the eerie feeling of running through a dark cave with only your own little light, so I'm planning to add more caves and some new mechanics. Next up are moths that swoop at your light, ledges that crumble under you, and updrafts you ride by holding the button.

comments.author: Fancy-Proof-9449
comments.body:
"Beatable isn't the same as fair" is the big one. I hit the same thing with my arcade game. The test bots reacted instantly and could zigzag in ways no thumb can, so they said levels were fine that real people couldn't get through.

What fixed it was a second, worse pilot made to play like a person: about a quarter second late on every reaction, eases the stick instead of snapping it, commits to a move instead of correcting every frame. Now the instant bot only tells me if something is possible, and the human-like one tells me if it's fair. Any clear rate from the fast bot is treated as a ceiling, never as the number.

Also +1 on playing every build yourself. The checks catch rules breaking, but only me playing tells me if it feels right.

replies.author: SvitsGames
replies.body: Yeah, tuning several bots for different kinds of players is a great idea.
